title: Introduction to Programming
description: An introduction to programming using Python. Students learn core constructs such as variables, control flow, functions and data structures, and apply them to solve small real-world problems while developing good habits in testing and code style.
learningOutcomes: Write, test and debug small programs using core programming constructs.
Select appropriate data structures to represent and manipulate data.
Decompose a problem into functions and explain the design choices made.
Apply basic testing techniques to check program correctness.

title: Database Systems
description: Covers the design and implementation of relational databases, from conceptual modelling to SQL and normalisation, with an introduction to transactions, indexing and the trade-offs of non-relational data stores.
learningOutcomes: Design a relational schema from a set of requirements using entity-relationship modelling.
Write SQL queries to create, update and retrieve data, including joins and aggregates.
Normalise a schema to third normal form and justify the result.
Explain how transactions and indexing affect consistency and performance.

title: Machine Learning
description: Introduces the principles and practice of machine learning, including supervised and unsupervised methods, model evaluation and the ethical issues raised by automated decision-making.
learningOutcomes: Explain the principles behind common supervised and unsupervised learning algorithms.
Train, tune and evaluate models using appropriate metrics and validation methods.
Critically assess the ethical and social implications of machine learning systems.

title: Computer Systems Fundamentals
description: Explores how computers work, from binary representation and logic gates to processor architecture, memory and operating systems.
